cim: Indiana University receives $25M from Lilly Endowment AI in Higher Ed initiative
cim_eredeti: Indiana University receives $25M from Lilly Endowment AI in Higher Ed initiative
szoveg_eredeti:
Lilly Endowment Inc. announced today that it will award Indiana University $25 million through its Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education initiative. IU is one of 35 colleges and universities in Indiana receiving funding through the initiative.

As a recipient of funding through the Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education initiative, IU will invest in new approaches to teaching, learning and student success. Photo by Chris Meyer, Indiana University

IU will use the funds to advance the Human + AI Learning Ecosystem, a transformational model for integrating artificial intelligence into undergraduate education and student support across the university’s nine campuses statewide. HALE builds on extensive planning and early institutional investments in AI tools, curriculum and faculty development to support the university’s efforts to implement AI in ways that strengthen learning and student success while meeting workforce needs.

“Indiana University is committed to preparing students to succeed in the careers of tomorrow and to navigate and shape a world being actively transformed by artificial intelligence,” IU President Pamela Whitten said. “As AI democratizes access to knowledge, great public universities like IU will focus on helping students develop the insight, judgment and innovation that will advance progress in Indiana and beyond. We are grateful that Lilly Endowment has invested in our work to advance a human-led, AI-enabled student experience.”

The co-principal investigators for the grant are Rahul Shrivastav, IU vice president for student success, and Anne Leftwich, chief academic and AI innovation officer. The HALE model was developed through a university-wide planning effort with four workstreams comprising more than 120 faculty, staff and students from across IU.

“Building on extensive planning and early institutional investments, HALE represents a coordinated approach to strengthening curriculum, faculty practice and student success systems at scale,” Shrivastav said. “Guided by the expertise of our faculty and strong engagement with the industry, this work will connect students to learning experiences and support that prepare them for an AI-enabled world.”

“Our goal isn’t simply to add AI to what we already do,” Leftwich said. “It’s to think carefully about what students need to learn, how teaching may need to change, and how we help students keep developing their own judgment, creativity and expertise. Students should know how to use AI well, but they also need the knowledge and confidence to question its output and make decisions for themselves.”

The Lilly Endowment Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education initiative is designed to help Indiana colleges and universities consider more fully the challenges and opportunities that artificial intelligence presents for their institutions and their students, as well as develop new or enhance existing strategies to improve their students’ educational opportunities and outcomes and their preparation to prosper in the workplace and life in a future that will be increasingly shaped by AI.

“The rapid rise and growing ubiquity of AI may be one of the most significant challenges higher education institutions have ever faced,” said Ted Maple, Lilly Endowment’s vice president for education. “Faculty and staff are concerned about the potential for AI to, among other things, impede original and independent thinking and threaten social connections. Yet at the same time, colleges and universities have recognized that AI may also present unprecedented opportunities for their institutions to enhance teaching and learning, student services, research capabilities and more. We are pleased to be able to help higher education institutions in Indiana find the best ways they can respond to these challenges and opportunities.”
